evidence.note: Keeps a rolling near-term list of remaining gaps (file attachments, leave route, IRC PRIVMSG, then SPA auth toggle, delete idempotency, restart, smoke tests) — subsystem-ish tracking of a few in-flight items, but never an explicit ledger over the full surface.

After a failed restart the terminal gets stuck; the agent repeats near-identical recovery attempts (Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D/Ctrl-U/echo RECOVERED) across ~8 steps without recognizing the circular state or changing tactics — a clear failure to detect a stuck/looping state.
Still thrashing with Ctrl-Z/Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D on the same stuck 'cat /tmp/huddle.log' line, continuing the loop rather than naming it and switching approach.

Multiple 'Mark task complete' submissions while step 19 admits the last health check 'did not complete cleanly'; finalizes without an accurate picture of what is verified vs broken, and whole families (search, groups, read-state, resilience, WS resume) are never tracked.

reasoning: Early on the agent shows a vague, rolling recollection of a handful of remaining fixes (anchor 3-5 territory), but it never maintains an explicit done/partial/failing status across the large contract surface and never cross-checks against the spec's many subsystems. Decisively, it fails the core stuck-state-detection aspect of this dimension: it repeats the same terminal-recovery action ~10 times across steps 9-20 without noticing the loop, and then finalizes despite acknowledging the state was unverified. That combination of only vague progress recall plus 'repeats the same failed fix without noticing' places it at a 3.
